# Column reference

<!-- Generated by docs/gen_columns.py from forster.template; do not edit by hand.
     Rerun `uv run python docs/gen_columns.py` after changing a column. -->

Every column FORSTER reads or writes, generated from the code
(`forster.template`). `forster template` writes the same tables into your folder as
`COLUMNS.md`. Fo is a fraction throughout (0.895, not 89.5). The desktop app shows
it in mol% and converts.

**Needed** says whether a column must be filled: *required*, *optional*, or *one
form*. Give fO2 either as `fO2_Pa` or as `fO2_buffer` with `fO2_delta_log`, and the
orientation either as `alpha_deg`, `beta_deg`, `gamma_deg` or as the four EBSD
columns (`phi1_deg`, `Phi_deg`, `phi2_deg`, `profile_angle_deg`). Leave the other
form empty.

Columns that hold several values (one per step, per segment or per growth stage)
take them in quotes, separated by commas: `"0.91, 0.89"`. An empty entry in such a
list (`"0.002, , 0.003"`) means "none for this one".

The pages [Setting up a run](setup.md) and [Reading the results](results.md) explain
what the columns change and how to read them.


## profiles.csv

One row per analysis point.

| Column | Unit | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profile` |  | required | Name of the profile. The `profile` column in parameters.csv refers to it. |
| `distance_um` | µm | required | Distance of the analysis point from the crystal edge. |
| `fo` | fraction | required | Forsterite content as a fraction, 0-1 (0.895, not 89.5). |
| `Marked_bad` |  | optional | `bad` leaves the point out of the fits. These are the points masked in the desktop app. |

## parameters.csv

One row per model run (one fit of one profile).

| Column | Unit | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run` |  | required | Name of the model run. It must be unique and names the output files. |
| `profile` |  | required | Name of the profile in profiles.csv to fit. |
| `T_C` | °C | required | Temperature. |
| `P_Pa` | Pa | required | Pressure (5e8 is 0.5 GPa). |
| `fO2_Pa` | Pa | one form | Oxygen fugacity. Alternatively, give the next two columns. |
| `fO2_buffer` |  | one form | Buffer: QFM (or FMQ) or NNO (Frost 1991). |
| `fO2_delta_log` | log units | one form | Offset of fO2 from that buffer. |
| `alpha_deg` | degrees | one form | Angle between the profile and [100]. |
| `beta_deg` | degrees | one form | Angle between the profile and [010]. |
| `gamma_deg` | degrees | one form | Angle between the profile and [001]. |
| `phi1_deg` | degrees | one form | EBSD Euler angle phi1 (Bunge). |
| `Phi_deg` | degrees | one form | EBSD Euler angle Phi (Bunge). |
| `phi2_deg` | degrees | one form | EBSD Euler angle phi2 (Bunge). |
| `profile_angle_deg` | degrees | one form | Direction of the profile on the EBSD map, measured from the positive x axis (east). |
| `domain_start_um` | µm | required | Start of the model domain, edge 1, where Fo is held (at edge1_fo). |
| `domain_end_um` | µm | required | End of the model domain, the far end. Fo is held there at the last segment's Fo (the core), unless centre_um is given. |
| `steps_um` | µm | required | Positions of the steps in the starting profile, in order: one number, or several in quotes ("10, 33"). The steps divide the profile into segments. |
| `segment_fo` | fraction | required | Starting Fo of each segment, from edge 1 inward. Give one more value than steps_um ("0.91, 0.89" for one step, "0.91, 0.93, 0.89" for two). Replaces edge_fo, core_fo and step_fo, which are still read until the release. |
| `segment_names` |  | optional | Labels for the segments, from edge 1 inward ("rim, mantle, core"). Empty: a, b, c, ... Joint fits match segments by label, and uncertainty results name them (a_fo, ...). |
| `edge1_fo` | fraction | optional | Fo held at edge 1 (domain_start_um) during diffusion, when it differs from the first segment's Fo. The first segment's Fo then stays the starting value. Empty: the first segment's Fo. With growth stages, it holds until the first stage. It cannot be combined with the initial-condition scan. Replaces rim_fo. |
| `centre_um` | µm | optional | Distance of the crystal's center, for modeling the whole crystal. The model runs to the center (beyond the measured points if needed) and mirrors the profile there, so no Fo crosses it and the core is free to change. Empty: a half profile, with the far end held at the core's Fo. Needs the implicit scheme and no growth stages. |
| `stage_days` | days | optional | Growth stages: the start of each stage, in days after the start of the run, one entry per stage ("2, 5" for two). At its start a stage moves the rim out to stage_rim_um, where a new zone of Fo stage_zone_fo appears and diffuses with the older crystal. The domain, step and Fo columns above describe the crystal before the first stage. Only times after the last stage are fitted, and time_days counts from the start. Needs dx_um and dt_s, the correlated uncertainty method, and no initial-condition scan (no _sd or _range columns). |
| `stage_rim_um` | µm | optional | Rim position from each stage on, one entry per stage. The crystal grows outward, so each value is at most the previous rim's (domain_start_um before the first stage). Keeping the previous rim changes only the rim's Fo (stage_rim_fo). Required with stage_days. |
| `stage_zone_fo` | fraction | optional | Fo of the zone each stage adds between the old and the new rim, one entry per stage. Every stage that moves the rim needs one. Leave an entry empty ("0.91, ") for a stage that only changes the rim's Fo. |
| `stage_rim_fo` | fraction | optional | Fo held at the rim from each stage on, one entry per stage. Empty, or an empty entry: that stage's stage_zone_fo. |
| `dx_um` | µm | optional | Grid spacing of the final fit. Leave it empty to have it chosen for about 1% accuracy in the fitted time. A value you give is kept, with a warning if it is coarse, wastefully fine, or too coarse for the steps. |
| `dt_s` | s | optional | Time step of the final fit, which sets how finely the fitted time is resolved. Leave it empty to have it chosen as 1/400 of the fitted time. The explicit schemes (central, dipra) split a dt above their stability limit (D dt / dx² = 0.5) into stable steps and keep only the rows at whole time steps. Growth stages need a stable dt, so they do not use the splitting. |
| `max_time_days` | days | optional | Longest time modeled. Default 200; with dx_um or dt_s empty, 3x a quick estimate of the time. |
| `scheme` |  | optional | implicit (default since 2026-10-13): rim on the end node, steps not snapped to nodes, any time step. central: the engine's explicit scheme, used before. dipra: DIPRA's forward-difference scheme (Girona and Costa 2013), a numerical scheme and not the diffusion law. With uncertainty = legacy the default is central. |
| `diffusivity` |  | optional | Fe-Mg diffusivity equation (the diffusion law). Choices: dipra: Classic DIPRA (Dohmen & Chakraborty 2007), preset dohmen_chakraborty2007; refit: FORSTER refit (2026), preset femg_refit2026; dfens_tamed: DFENS TaMED (Mutch et al. 2019), preset mutch2019_tamed; dfens_global: DFENS Global (Mutch et al. 2019), preset mutch2019_global. dipra is the default. Every choice but dipra carries a covariance, which adds the law_ range to summary.csv. refit also carries the spread between laboratories (the all_ range). Any other preset name also works, as does a name from diffusivities.csv (then run forster fit with --diffusivities). |
| `uncertainty` |  | optional | correlated (default) or legacy (the round robin rule, which reproduces old results). |
| `steps_sd_um` | µm | optional | Uncertainty on the step position(s), as a Gaussian 1 sigma: one value, or one per step ("2, 5"). 0 keeps a step fixed. Alternatively, give steps_range_um. |
| `steps_range_um` | µm | optional | Uncertainty on the step position(s) as a uniform ± half-width, in the same form as steps_sd_um. |
| `segment_fo_sd` | fraction | optional | Uncertainty on each segment's Fo, as a Gaussian 1 sigma: one value for every segment, or one per segment ("0.002, , 0.003"). Empty or 0 keeps a segment fixed. Replaces edge_fo_sd, core_fo_sd and step_fo_sd. |
| `segment_fo_range` | fraction | optional | Uncertainty on each segment's Fo as a uniform ± half-width, in the same form as segment_fo_sd. A segment may take one of the two, not both. |
| `scan_method` |  | optional | How the uncertain starting-profile parameters are fitted. auto (default) finds the best fit, then uses importance sampling from a Laplace proposal, or nested sampling when that has too few effective samples. The other choices are laplace, nested, and grid (every node of a grid, as before 2026-10-15). Blank with scan_points given means grid. |
| `scan_seed` |  | optional | Seed of the sampler (default 0). The same seed gives the same result. |
| `scan_points` |  | optional | For scan_method grid, the points per uncertain parameter (default 13 for one, 9 for two, 5 for more). |
| `scan_dx_um` | µm | optional | Grid spacing of the scan's runs. Empty: chosen for about 5% accuracy, which is coarser and faster than the final fit. |
| `scan_dt_s` | s | optional | Time step of the scan's runs. Empty: 1/80 of the nominal fit's time. For central or dipra it is raised, if needed, to the step at which the fastest candidate reaches D dt / dx² = 0.4. |
| `scan_max_time_days` | days | optional | Longest time the scan's runs model. Empty: max_time_days if given, capped at 10x the fitted time, otherwise 3x the fitted time. A warning says if the posterior of time reaches the end. |
| `mc_T_sd_C` | °C | optional | Monte Carlo over the conditions and the diffusion law (forster.rescale), run when any mc_ spread column is given. This column is the 1 sigma of temperature. |
| `mc_P_sd_Pa` | Pa | optional | Monte Carlo: 1 sigma of pressure. |
| `mc_fO2_sd_log` | log10 | optional | Monte Carlo: 1 sigma of log10 fO2 (relative to mc_fO2_buffer when given). |
| `mc_fO2_buffer` |  | optional | Monte Carlo: QFM or NNO, to hold fO2 relative to that buffer so it follows each draw's T and P. Empty: the row's fO2_buffer when fO2 is given that way, otherwise fO2 is drawn on its own. |
| `mc_law` |  | optional | Monte Carlo: yes (default) draws the diffusion law's parameters from its covariance, or no. Laws without a covariance, such as dipra, are exact. |
| `mc_between_study` |  | optional | Monte Carlo: yes adds the spread between laboratories (for an absolute time). Default no. |
| `mc_samples` |  | optional | Monte Carlo draws (default 4000; 200 refits for runs with growth stages). |
| `mc_seed` |  | optional | Monte Carlo seed (default 0). |
| `crystal` |  | optional | Name of the crystal this profile was measured on. Runs with the same crystal will be fitted jointly, with a shared time and compositions and their own steps. For now the name is only carried through. The joint fit exists from Python (forster.fit_crystal), and tables and the CLI are planned (docs/plans/2026-10-16-joint-fits.md). |
| `sample` |  | optional | Name of the sample (rock) the crystal comes from. Crystals of one sample form the population for priors on segment Fo. Carried through for now. |
| `notes` |  | optional | Free text for your own records. |

## diffusivities.csv

Optional. Use it for your own diffusivity equations, one row per equation. Name an equation in the `diffusivity` column of parameters.csv and pass the table to `forster fit` with `--diffusivities`. For each crystal axis i ([100], [010], [001]):

`log10 D_i = log10_D0_i + fO2_exponent log10(fO2 / fO2_ref_Pa) + fo_coefficient (fo_ref - X_Fo) - (E_i + activation_volume_m3_mol (P - P_ref_Pa)) / (ln(10) R T) + pressure_coefficient_per_Pa (P - P_ref_Pa)`

with T in K, P and fO2 in Pa and R = 8.3145 J/mol/K. Along the profile, D is the sum of D_i cos²(angle to axis i). The table `forster template` writes holds the built-in equations; copy a row, give it a new name and change the values.

| Column | Unit | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` |  | required | Name to use in the `diffusivity` column of parameters.csv. |
| `element` |  | required | Fe-Mg for fits. Ni, Mn and Ca are listed for reference. |
| `log10_D0_100` | log10 m²/s | required | Pre-factor along [100]. |
| `log10_D0_010` | log10 m²/s | required | Pre-factor along [010]. |
| `log10_D0_001` | log10 m²/s | required | Pre-factor along [001]. |
| `E_100_J_mol` | J/mol | required | Activation energy along [100]. |
| `E_010_J_mol` | J/mol | required | Activation energy along [010]. |
| `E_001_J_mol` | J/mol | required | Activation energy along [001]. |
| `fO2_exponent` |  | required | Exponent n of (fO2 / fO2_ref_Pa). |
| `fO2_ref_Pa` | Pa | required | Reference fO2 (1e5 if the equation uses bar). |
| `fo_coefficient` | log10 per unit Fo | required | The coefficient m in m (fo_ref - X_Fo). Use 0 for none. |
| `fo_ref` | fraction | required | Reference Fo of the composition term. |
| `activation_volume_m3_mol` | m³/mol | required | Activation volume (0 for none). |
| `P_ref_Pa` | Pa | required | Reference pressure of the pressure terms. |
| `pressure_coefficient_per_Pa` | log10 per Pa | required | Pressure term outside the exponential (0 for none). |
| `source` |  | optional | Where the equation comes from. |

## summary.csv

Written by `forster fit` and by the app's Export. It has one row per fitted run, with `run`, `profile`, the results below and every parameter column above (fO2 in Pa, orientation as angles). You can read it back as a parameter table to repeat the fits.

| Column | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `diffusivity_label` |  | Display name of the diffusivity equation. The diffusivity column holds its preset name. |
| `time_days` | days | Best-fit time. |
| `time_since_last_stage_days` | days | Best-fit time since the start of the last growth stage (stage_days). Without stages it equals time_days. |
| `low_days` | days | Low end of the 1-sigma range. |
| `high_days` | days | High end of the 1-sigma range. |
| `low2_days` | days | Low end of the 2-sigma range (95.45%). Empty for the legacy method. |
| `high2_days` | days | High end of the 2-sigma range. |
| `law_sigma_log10` | log10 | 1 sigma of log10 D from the diffusion law's covariance at the run's conditions (also the 1 sigma of log10 time, with the sign changed). Empty for laws without a covariance (the default) and for fits with growth stages or a rim value that changes in time (docs/references/law-uncertainty-limits.md). |
| `between_study_log10` | log10 | Spread between laboratories in the law's calibration data (a random study offset). |
| `law_low_days` | days | Low end of the 1-sigma range with the law's uncertainty added. To compare crystals fitted with the same law, use low_days and high_days, because the law's error is common to all of them. For a time on its own, use these. |
| `law_high_days` | days | High end of that range. |
| `all_low_days` | days | Low end of the range with the spread between laboratories added as well. Use it for an absolute time, if the crystal may sit off the laboratories' average as one more experiment would. |
| `all_high_days` | days | High end of that range. |
| `reduced_chi2` |  | Chi-squared at the best fit over (points fitted - 1). It is a diagnostic only. For the correlated method it is about 1 by construction, because the noise model is fitted to the residuals. For legacy it is taken over the kriged grid points, so the two are not comparable. Judge correlated fits by the three noise columns. |
| `points_fitted` |  | Measured points inside the model domain (legacy: kriged grid points). |
| `white_sigma_fo` | fraction | Fitted scatter of the points (correlated method). A value much larger than your analytical precision points to outliers or an underestimated precision. |
| `correlated_sigma_fo` | fraction | Fitted smooth misfit between model and data. If it is large next to white_sigma_fo, the model misses the shape of the profile, so check the starting profile. |
| `correlation_length_um` | µm | Length scale of that misfit. Near half the profile length, the misfit spans the whole profile. |
| `near_step_daic` |  | AIC change when the misfit may be larger near the steps (correlated method, no growth stages). Below -6 a warning says the misfit is concentrated near the step and the 1-sigma range is probably too narrow (docs/references/noise-models-guide.md). |
| `near_step_misfit_sigma_fo` | fraction | Standard deviation of the near-step model's misfit at the step, which shows how large the misfit is there (0.001 = 0.1 mol% Fo). |
| `near_step_points` |  | Measured points within 2 diffusion lengths of a step (-1: check not run). With fewer than about 13 the check often misses a near-step misfit, so a silent check is weak evidence. Quote the 2-sigma range then. |
| `core_end_diffusion_lengths` |  | Distance from the last step to the model's core end (the last measured point), in diffusion lengths at the best fit. The core Fo is held there. Below 3 a warning says the data probably stop at or before the plateau, which moves the fit (docs/guide/practical-advice.md). |
| `points_outside_domain` |  | Measured points before domain_start_um or past domain_end_um, which are not fitted. This is often deliberate, for example to leave out an earlier stage. If the points continue a flat plateau, extending the domain to include them makes the near-step check more reliable. |
| `warnings` |  | Warnings from the fit, such as a range that reaches the last time step. |
| `forster_version` |  | FORSTER version that made the fit. |
| `scan_best_days` | days | With uncertainties: best-fit time over all scanned initial conditions. With the sampled methods, the time of the best-fit initial condition. |
| `scan_sampler` |  | Method that produced the scan columns: grid, laplace or nested. auto runs laplace and falls back to nested. |
| `scan_median_days` | days | Sampled methods: median of the posterior of time over the initial-condition parameters. |
| `scan_low_days` | days | Low end of the 1-sigma range including the initial-condition uncertainty. For grid it is the profile likelihood, and for the sampled methods the central 68% of the posterior of time. |
| `scan_high_days` | days | High end of that range. |
| `scan_marginal_low_days` | days | Low end of the Bayesian (marginal) range. With Gaussian uncertainties it is pulled toward the nominal initial condition. |
| `scan_marginal_high_days` | days | High end of the Bayesian range. |
| `scan_best` |  | Best values of the scanned parameters (step1_um, a_fo, ...). The nominal values stay in the parameter columns. |
| `scan_candidates` |  | Initial conditions fitted (one model run each). |
| `scan_ic_share` |  | Sampled methods: fraction of the variance of time that comes from the choice of initial condition. The rest is the fit at a fixed initial condition. |
| `scan_sensitivity` |  | Sampled methods: change of the expected time per unit of each parameter, from the posterior samples (days per µm for steps, days per unit Fo fraction). |
| `scan_ess` |  | Sampled methods: effective sample size of the importance samples (out of 1024). Below 256, auto uses nested sampling. |
| `scan_log_evidence` |  | Sampled methods: log evidence. Use it to compare initial-condition models (one step or two) fitted to the same profile with the same grid. |
| `scan_prior_offsets` |  | Distance of each fitted starting-profile value from its nominal value, in prior units (sd for _sd, half-width for _range). For example, a_fo=+2.30 is 2.3 sd above. From 2 sd (short of the prior's edge at 2.5) a warning says the prior and the data disagree. |
| `scan_near_step_daic` |  | near_step_daic at the best-fit initial condition. Fitting the initial condition usually clears a near-step warning. If it is still below -6, the misfit is concentrated near the step, so quote the 2-sigma range. |
| `mc_method` |  | Monte Carlo method: rescale (t = t_fit D_fit / D_draw, exact for a fixed rim) or refit (for growth stages, every draw is refitted). |
| `mc_draws` |  | Monte Carlo draws made. |
| `mc_median_days` | days | Monte Carlo median time, combining the fit (or the initial-condition posterior), the conditions and the diffusion law. |
| `mc_low_days` | days | Monte Carlo 16th percentile. |
| `mc_high_days` | days | Monte Carlo 84th percentile. |
| `mc_p05_days` | days | Monte Carlo 5th percentile. |
| `mc_p95_days` | days | Monte Carlo 95th percentile. |
| `mc_sd_log10` | log10 | Monte Carlo: standard deviation of log10 time from each source drawn alone (fit, T, P, fO2, law, studies). It shows which source matters most. |
| `scan_dropped` |  | Grid points left out as invalid (steps out of order or outside the domain, Fo outside 0-1). |
| `grid_resolution` |  | Diffusion length sqrt(D t) at the fit over the grid spacing. For 1% accuracy in the fitted time it should be about 5 (implicit) or 240 (central, dipra). |
| `grid_error_pct` | % | Estimated worst-case error of the fitted time from the grid spacing: 0.2 x (dx / l)² for implicit, 2.4 x dx / l for central and dipra, where l is the diffusion length (measured on 35 real profiles). |
| `grid_stability` |  | D dt / dx² of the final fit's time step. For central and dipra, above 0.5 each step is split into stable steps. Empty for implicit. |
